title.narrative: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Dev. (ICIMOD), 2023-2026
International Centre for Integrated Mountain Dev. (ICIMOD), 2023-2026

description.narrative: ICIMOD arbetar för att uppnå en grönare, mer inkluderande och mer klimatresilient Hindu Kush Himalaya-region. Sida stödjer genomförandet av deras handlingsplan Mid-term Action Plan 2023-2026.
ICIMOD works to achieve a greener, more inclusive, and climate resilient Hindu Kush Himalaya. Sida supports the implementation of ICIMOD's Mid-term Action Plan 2023-2026.

In ICIMOD's fifth mid-term action plan (MTAP V) for the period 2023-2026 their work is divided into three strategic groups and six action areas/objectives:
Strategic group 1: REDUCING CLIMATE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS: Action area A) Managing cryosphere and water risks Action area B) Stimulating action for clean air
Strategic group 2: SHAPING GREEN AND RESILIENT MOUNTAIN ECONOMIES: Action area C) Adapting and transforming livelihoods and economies Action area D) Restoring and regenerating landscapes
Strategic group 3: ENABLING REGIONAL AND GLOBAL MECHANISMS FOR SUSTAINABLE ACTION: Action area E) Building institutions for regional cooperation and collaboration Action area F) Strengthening global leadership in sustainable mountain development

In 2024 (based on latest annual report) ICIMOD for example achieved the following results:
The SERVIRHKH collaboration continued developing early warning tools such as customised weather forecast models and warning systems (Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan) and flood alerts through phone applications.
ICIMOD assisted local governments in Nepal (Koshi River Basin) in embracing gender sensitive disaster planning and budgeting in the subnational Treasury Regulatory Application (SuTRA).
ICIMOD provided data and built awareness of the accelerating rates of cryosphere change, whilst enhancing institutional capability and individual capacity for cryosphere science and analysis, in the RMCs. They introduced measures to enhance national permafrost and glacier monitoring capacity in Bhutan and Nepal, continued to support Masters programme in Kathmandu University and launched the HKH Women on Ice initiative.
ICIMOD combined air quality data from stations with satellite imagery and generated new simulations to identify and locate pollutants at finer scales, and to start to correlate these with health impacts. They convened regional workshops on environmental dust and black carbon (BC) monitoring, creating a dashboard and satellite model based products for regional partners, which are enabling RMCs to adopt a standardised methodology for regional air quality monitoring.
ICIMOD contributed foresight assessments, and helped identify opportunities for livelihoods, including through migration, settlements and renewable energy. Developing climateresilient agroecology in Nepal led to the successful establishment of new Community Learning Centres (CLCs), an approach which was adopted into strategy and budget of local government (Karnali Province).
ICIMOD supported women and youth in green entrepreneurship and promoted the productive use of renewable energy in powering mountain economies.
ICIMODs presence in essential sciencepolicy fora contributed to inserting HKH issues and needs into key statements and documents, thus helping ensure the HKH is reflected and primed to trigger potential actions on increased investment flows into the region. In 2024, ICIMOD successfully engaged with RMC focal points to promote mountain needs and perspectives in global fora (UNFCCC, CBD, IPCC and IPBES).
Following the approval of the GESI Policy, specific GESI makers introduced and the GESI Capacity Development Manual was developed and staff training on GESI mainstreaming delivered. The Overarching Safeguarding Policy was drafted, incorporating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for child safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and sexual harassment and eight safeguarding training sessions for staff were conducted.
ICIMOD made several institutional process improvements, firstly ensuring independence of the Evaluation & Learning function, with a new Evaluation Policy approved, and a new Independent Evaluation Unit established. They brought together several functions into a new Strategic Results, Partnership, and Business Development (SRPBD) Unit.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
